markdown_report:
The best next experiment remains **freshness-weighted recurring-interest pooling**, interpreted precisely as *later-endpoint freshness*. At 10% progress, this small extension is feasible, but its main challenge is distinguishing refreshed recurrence from stronger ordinary recency.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) A zero-initialized bounded residual preserves initial SASRec predictions. It does not guarantee improved ranking. (2) Distinct IDs establish lexical corroboration, not independent evidence, compatibility, or unmet demand. Duplicate products remain possible [4]. (3) The proposed factor ages the later endpoint of a pair. With exclusively earlier witnesses, it reduces exactly to stronger anchor decay; later witnesses provide the distinctive refresh mechanism.

**Insights from related work.** (1) Intent research motivates temporal modeling without establishing observed intent [1]. TiSASRec and MEANTIME distinguish elapsed-time relationships from sequence positions [5,6]. (2) History interventions measure recommendation dependence [2]. Matched edits cannot identify causal preferences. (3) Sampled evaluation can change model ordering [3]. Training margins and full-catalog audits therefore remain separate from selection.

These insights organize three directions: temporal identification, conservative integration, and controlled evaluation. The conceptual matrix is:

| Method | Evidence | Temporal treatment | Integration |
|---|---|---|---|
| SASRec | Learned interactions | Causal positions | Backbone |
| Starting residual | Historical lexical recurrence | Anchor recency | Bounded feature addition |
| Proposed residual | Same recurrence | Anchor and later-endpoint recency | Same bounded addition |

Three atomic ideas follow. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Freshness-weighted corroboration [1,2,5,6] | 3/6/5 | Originality: explicit refresh hypothesis; potential: falsifiable temporal mechanism; difficulty: preserves tensor interface | Originality: established decay primitives; potential: stronger recency may explain gains; difficulty: exact causal computation and controls |
| Duplicate-document witness exclusion [4] | 3/6/4 | Originality: focused control; potential: tests redundant evidence; difficulty: deterministic grouping | Originality: standard deduplication; potential: removes valid variants; difficulty: grouping choices |
| Fixed lexical-hard diagnostic panel [3] | 3/6/3 | Originality: combines probes; potential: exposes confusing candidates; difficulty: unchanged architecture | Originality: diagnostic contribution; potential: no direct accuracy mechanism; difficulty: potentially relevant distractors |

For the selected idea, multiply similarity by later-endpoint freshness *inside* the causal maximum. Preserve denominator shrinkage, downward clipping, and the zero-initialized gate. Compare SASRec, the original residual, and the freshness residual; add an anchor-only decay control at the algebraically matched timescale. Independently tuned anchor decay is necessary before attributing gains to refresh rather than recency; equal tuning opportunities must fit the budget.

Keep all four routes, seeds 0/42, the 200-epoch environment default, serialization, and diagnostic interfaces. Select solely through pinned macro validation HR@10. Verify causal-reference agreement and exported predictor parity; report coverage, gate signs, residual magnitude, runtime, and incomplete controls. Audit duplicate text and use affordable shuffled-text controls. No validation improvement is established; persistent interests, lexical shortcuts, and adaptive selection remain risks.

References: [1] https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.16350 ; [2] https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03606 ; [3] https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.13045 ; [4] https://www.kbs.uni-hannover.de/~ntoutsi/papers/17.SDM.pdf ; [5] https://jiachengli1995.github.io/files/wsdm20.pdf ; [6] https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.08273

idea.description: Add later-endpoint freshness attenuation to the starting confidence-aware recurring-interest residual. Historical anchors receive support from similar distinct historical items, with each pair attenuated by the age of its more recent endpoint. Test whether later corroboration refreshing older anchors contributes beyond stronger anchor recency.
idea.motivation: The qualitative audit identifies outdated historical associations as a possible failure mode, but neither current demand nor validation benefit is observed. The proposed operator is not pure witness freshness: a newly occurring anchor receives unattenuated corroboration from an old witness. For earlier witnesses only, its temporal factors collapse to stronger anchor decay. The experiment therefore tests a narrow refresh hypothesis against explicit recency controls rather than treating any gain as evidence of intent understanding.
idea.implementation_notes:
This is a research intervention specification, not an executable replacement train.py: the baseline source and predictor entry-point signature were not supplied. No experiments or source inspection were performed. Retain DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], all four independent dataset routes, unchanged splits, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, single-GPU execution, and SASREC_EPOCHS environment default 200. Write every artifact beneath the trial directory. Use only public titles, descriptions, histories, and timestamps; ignore the conflicting illustrative schema for unavailable fields. Do not infer ownership, satisfied demand, compatibility, diversity preferences, or conformity.

Reuse the starting residual's fixed training-item TF-IDF. To remove ambiguity, concatenate deterministically flattened title and description strings with a space; fit once per category on unique training-history items in saved item-ID order. Use TfidfVectorizer(dtype=float32, lowercase=True, analyzer='word', ngram_range=(1,1), max_features=20000, min_df=1, smooth_idf=True, norm='l2', stop_words=None, sublinear_tf=False, token_pattern=r'(?u)\b\w\w+\b'). Save vocabulary, IDF, CSR vectors, item mapping, configuration, and dependency versions. Missing or nontraining-item vectors are zero; an empty vocabulary disables the branch. Freeze these artifacts and share them across temporal arms.

Fix threshold theta=0.1, denominator offset kappa=1, rho_anchor=10, rho_witness=10, residual coefficient bound 0.25, and epsilon=1e-8 as initial hypotheses. Indices refer to the baseline's retained sequence positions, not elapsed time. For nonpadding anchor i at prefix t, maximize S(i,j)*exp(-(t-max(i,j))/rho_witness) over nonpadding j<=t with different item IDs and abs(i-j)>=3, where S=max(cosine-theta,0). Multiply by exp(-(t-i)/rho_anchor). Empty support is exactly zero. This measures interaction-position freshness, not calendar freshness or pairwise temporal separation. Preserve chronological occurrences; repeated IDs cannot corroborate one another, but multiple occurrences can still increase aggregate pooling mass.

For j<=i, the combined decay equals exp(-(t-i)/rho_eff), where 1/rho_eff=1/rho_anchor+1/rho_witness; the proposed defaults give rho_eff=5. Only later witnesses distinguish the operator from this reduction. A recent anchor with an ancient witness has pair freshness one, although the spacing constraint still applies. Report these behaviors explicitly. If actual witness age is desired instead, exp(-(t-j)/rho_witness) defines a different experiment and must not be silently substituted.

Compute p=sum_i(weight_i*embedding_i)/(1+sum_i(weight_i)), then multiply p by min(1,stop_gradient(norm(h))/(norm(p)+epsilon)). Never normalize weak support upward. Return h+0.25*tanh(g)*p with one scalar g=0 per category. Empty support returns exactly zero. The cap bounds residual norm relative to the current backbone feature but does not calibrate relevance or confidence. Negative learned gates are permitted and must be reported. Preserve the baseline objective, optimizer, batching, sampler, initialization, and checkpoint protocol for the first comparisons.

Use sequence-local sparse text products, avoiding catalog-by-catalog similarities. The pseudocode is a correctness oracle. For a fixed retained window, an exact vectorized implementation can use transformed keys S(i,j)*exp(max(i,j)/rho_witness) with a cumulative maximum over j, followed by exp(-t/rho_witness), causal masks, and anchor decay. Rebase indices to the local window and use float64 intermediate keys or log-domain comparisons to avoid overflow; zero scores have log key negative infinity. Verify final float32 outputs against the oracle. The support and embedding aggregation cost O(BL²) and O(BL²d), respectively, excluding sparse similarity construction. Never build a B x L x L x L tensor.

If inference instead maintains sliding state, a single maximum per anchor is insufficient when its winning witness expires. Recompute from the retained window initially. An optional optimized implementation uses one monotone deque per active anchor, inserts eligible partners with key log(S(i,j))+max(i,j)/rho_witness, removes dominated tails and expired heads, and drops expired anchors. Initialize a new anchor with all eligible historical partners, preserving expiration backups. Masks must precede insertion. This requires O(TW) pair processing and O(W²) worst-case state, excluding similarities; it is not constant-cost recommendation. Lemire supplies the deque primitive, not this recommender derivation. Do not introduce streaming until parity with recomputation is established.

Prespecify matched SASRec, original-residual rho_anchor=10, freshness-residual 10/10, and original-residual rho_anchor=5 arms, retaining all four categories in every arm. The rho=5 control matches the earlier-witness algebra but does not equalize residual magnitudes automatically because maxima, mass shrinkage, and clipping interact. Report support mass and residual-to-feature norm in all arms. Before claiming a refresh mechanism, compare against independently tuned anchor-only decay under equal validation queries and training/checkpoint opportunities; if that comparison cannot fit, report the attribution as unresolved. Static semantic gating, pair-distance decay, witness-age decay, and last-item or recency-only pooling are separately budgeted alternatives, not mandatory additions to the initial search.

Reserve whole-text permutation only if profiling shows it fits: use seed 0 to permute training-item documents within category and training-derived popularity, text-length, and missingness strata; preserve empty documents, save the permutation, and report singleton strata and the fraction reassigned. Refit the same TF-IDF specification for that control. Audit exact normalized-document duplicates using deterministic whitespace normalization and case folding, with empty documents excluded from duplicate groups. Distinct IDs do not establish distinct products. Title-only, description-only, template removal, and near-duplicate grouping introduce additional factors and require declared rules and budget. Report lexical support coverage and descriptive results by training frequency, history length, and text availability with counts. A surviving shuffled-text benefit weakens semantic interpretation but does not by itself identify its alternative cause. Candidate-permuted scalar corrections from the supplied search suggestions do not directly preserve this feature-residual mechanism and are not a primary matched control.

Keep log2feats tensor-shaped B x L x D and predict_score compatible with supplied B x L items. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions; view.model must be the actual trained module, and item_emb the trained embedding table. Retain user_train, meta_data, and review_data interfaces, leaving unavailable fields unavailable. Restore all module modes and Python, NumPy, Torch, and initialized CUDA RNG states after diagnostics. Retain embedding alignment, training margins, finite coverage, causal checks, and compatibility-view parity as descriptive probes. Add original-versus-fresh support mass, supported-position count, distinct supported-ID count, later-witness winning fraction, gate sign, and residual-norm summaries. Define the later-witness statistic using deterministic smallest-index tie breaking and exclude zero-support anchors. These are mechanism diagnostics, not relevance metrics.

Update the predictor writer so working/predict.py restores identical text state, mapping, architecture, gates, retained-window logic, padding, positional convention, and pooling. Verify the optimized implementation against the naive oracle on repeated IDs, padding, empty text, short prefixes, zero support, all-padding rows, expired windows, ties, and position-preserving future masking. Check the earlier-witness algebra directly. Verify serialized predictor scores with atol=1e-5 and rtol=1e-4, plus ranking agreement under consistent tie handling, across every dataset route. Compatibility-view parity alone does not verify export parity. For inference-removal probes keep candidate identities fixed; these measure model dependence. Matched retraining assesses incremental predictive benefit.

Record resolved settings, arm order, checkpoint opportunities, attempted configurations, failures, runtime estimates, and GPU-second allocations before execution. Charge profiling, diagnostics, failures, tuning, and all attempted trials to 43,200 GPU-seconds; four concurrent slots do not increase that shared allowance. Do not assume the complete control menu fits or reduce a losing control's allowance after observing scores. Select only by host macro validation HR@10 with 200 users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, and evaluation seed 42. Preserve host splits and candidates. If aligned per-user validation hits are exposed, report paired macro differences using 10,000 within-category bootstrap resamples with seed 42 and percentile 95% intervals. These condition on selected fitted models and fixed candidates, excluding training variability and adaptive-selection bias; otherwise omit intervals. Freeze the final choice before held-out evaluation.

Full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for five real training users per category remain descriptive simulator inputs. Exclude padding and previously seen items, score in chunks, and check chunk invariance. Preserve unknown compatibility and demand judgments, supporting qualitative claims only with available histories, timestamps, and exact public-text excerpts. No validation improvement is established by the supplied training diagnostics. No hidden test access, external data, pretrained weights, evaluator changes, fabricated metrics, or multi-GPU execution.
idea.pseudocode:
DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']
# Preserve baseline routes, splits, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42.
# Declare affordable arms and identical checkpoint opportunities before execution.
for dataset in FOUR_DATASETS:
    text = load_or_fit_fixed_training_item_tfidf(dataset)
    model = baseline_SASRec_with_identical_initialization()
    g = Parameter(0.0)
    for sequence, positive, negative in baseline_training_batches:
        h = causal_SASRec(sequence)              # B x L x D
        e = item_emb(sequence)
        for batch row b:
            for nonpadding prefix position t:
                weights = zeros(L)
                for nonpadding anchor i <= t:
                    support = 0.0
                    for nonpadding witness j <= t:
                        if sequence[b,i] != sequence[b,j] and abs(i-j) >= 3:
                            S = max(cosine(text[sequence[b,i]],
                                           text[sequence[b,j]]) - 0.1, 0.0)
                            pair_freshness = exp(-(t-max(i,j))/10.0)
                            support = max(support, S*pair_freshness)
                    weights[i] = support*exp(-(t-i)/10.0)
                p = sum_i(weights[i]*e[b,i])/(1.0+sum(weights))
                p *= min(1.0, stop_gradient(norm(h[b,t]))/(norm(p)+1e-8))
                features[b,t] = h[b,t]+0.25*tanh(g)*p
        optimize_unchanged_baseline_loss(features, positive, negative)
    serialize_model_text_mapping_configuration_and_gate()
    export_identical_predictor_logic()
    verify_oracle_causality_reload_score_and_ranking_parity()

# Controls reuse identical text, residual construction, and training protocol:
# SASRec; original residual with anchor rho=10; proposed 10/10;
# original residual with anchor rho=5.
# For earlier witnesses only: rho_eff=(1/10+1/10)^(-1)=5.
# Tune anchor-only decay with equal opportunities before asserting refresh benefit.
# Run shuffled-text and further controls only within predeclared shared budget.
# Select solely through pinned four-category macro validation HR@10.
# Report missing controls and unresolved mechanism claims.

originality.positive: Specifies an identifiable later-witness refresh mechanism and an exact algebraic control that makes the hypothesis falsifiable.
originality.negative: Semantic pooling, temporal decay, gating, and streaming maxima are established primitives. Earlier-witness contributions reduce to stronger ordinary recency, and exact-combination novelty is unverified.

future_potential.positive: A controlled comparison could clarify whether refreshed historical corroboration contributes beyond ordinary recency while preserving the existing scoring interface.
future_potential.negative: Persistent interests may benefit from old evidence; duplicate products, boilerplate, sparse text coverage, and popularity correlations can explain apparent gains. The operator does not establish current demand.

code_difficulty.positive: Adds one trainable scalar per category and retains tensor-valued features, the scoring head, and the diagnostic compatibility contract.
code_difficulty.negative: Exact causal support, sparse similarity costs, expiration-safe optimization, matched temporal controls, artifact serialization, and exported predictor parity require moderate implementation and runtime effort.

related_work.title: Intent-aware recommendation survey (supplied search reference)
contributions: Discusses changing recommendation intent across visits and within sessions, motivating temporal evidence modeling.
limitations: Does not establish that lexical recurrence measures current intent or that the proposed residual improves this benchmark.

related_work.title: History-edit interventions for sequential recommendations, Scarcelli et al. (2025; supplied reference)
contributions: Searches for minimal history edits that change sequential recommendations, motivating controlled dependence tests.
limitations: Recommendation sensitivity under edits does not identify causal user preferences or validate freshness weighting.

related_work.title: Sampled evaluation and sequential recommendation rankings, Dallmann et al. (supplied reference)
contributions: Reports inconsistencies between sampled-candidate and full-catalog model rankings.
limitations: Does not justify changing the pinned evaluator; full-catalog audits and sampled HR@10 answer different questions.

related_work.title: Amazon item-variant redundancy study, Basaran, Ntoutsi and Zimek (SDM 2017; supplied reference)
contributions: Shows that redundant Amazon item variants can distort recommendation evaluation, motivating duplicate-group audits.
limitations: Does not establish description boilerplate as the mechanism or validate a particular TF-IDF deduplication rule.

related_work.title: TiSASRec: Time Interval Aware Self-Attention for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Separates positional information from pairwise elapsed-time intervals using learned temporal embeddings.
Provides position-only, interval-only, and combined comparisons.
limitations: Learned interval embeddings are not monotone freshness decay and do not validate recurring-interest corroboration.
Reported results use different experimental settings.

related_work.title: MEANTIME: Mixture of Attention Mechanisms with Multi-temporal Embeddings for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Combines multiple temporal encodings, including exponential pairwise-time kernels.
Reports dataset-dependent effects of temporal embedding combinations.
limitations: Pairwise temporal separation differs from the age of a pair's later endpoint.
Does not establish the proposed lexical refresh mechanism.

related_work.title: Streaming Maximum-Minimum Filter Using No More than Three Comparisons per Element, Lemire
contributions: Provides a monotone-deque primitive for streaming extrema that can support expiration-aware maxima.
limitations: The per-anchor transformed-score recurrence is a separate derivation.
Amortized deque operations do not eliminate processing across all active anchors or quadratic worst-case state.
